label: his When Healing Turns Into Checking P3, as he pasted it
his: And the checking doesn't always stay in your head. A body scan can turn into one, or a confession. Even, going on a date, or checking your dating profile matches, can be a version of this if what you're really after is proof that you're good and lovable. It might calm things down for a while, and then the next little wobble matters even more.

label: his Finding a Therapist P2
his: Inner Child Reparenting therapists do exist, and you can find them, although they often are not licensed, and I don't know of any central directory, nor of any protocol they'd have in common. There are none which work with my guide yet. I can consult, and if you like the guide, you can ask a therapist to check it out and see what they agree with or disagree with as a great way to vet them.

label: his Finding a Therapist P3 (his two links of 2026-10-18 kept)
his: The best licensed, listed therapists you'll find that come close will be doing Internal Family Systems (IFS), or Schema Therapy. I'll talk more about those next, but Schema Therapy comes closest to my approach. [Open Path Collective](https://openpathcollective.org/pricing-and-eligibility-for-affordable-therapy/) (or a similar resource in your country) lists thousands of affordable therapists. You can filter them by Schema or IFS. You can often find [even more Schema therapists at the official site](https://schematherapysociety.org/Search?&tab=1).

label: his Finding a Therapist P4
his: Before choosing a therapist, get to know the strengths and pitfalls of their approach, including any modifications they make to the standard protocol. I'd especially want to interview them regarding how they treat spiritual experiences. You want someone who won't tell you what yours really mean, downplay them, force them, or treat them as a symptom. What have they found too challenging to deal with so far, and where have they seen the best results? A good therapist won't charge you an arm and a leg just for this kind of interview, and they should already have this information on their website to avoid wasting too much time. A certificate on the wall can't tell you any of that.

label: his Finding a Therapist P5
his: Regarding AI therapy, I've tried all the top AI therapy apps, and they're all pretty bad. I'm trying to make my own based on this guide, but I'm becoming more convinced that unsupervised AI therapy is just a toss up. That doesn't mean you can't get a lot of great insights sometimes when talking to AI, though, but just expect it to go sideways sometimes.
